_comment: Copy this file to logsources.json (git-ignored) and describe your own servers, or edit it on the GUI's Log sources page. --server-log streams these into each session's panel and keeps each scenario's slice next to the screenshots in the report. Connections say WHERE to run a reader; logs say WHAT to read. One connection serves every log on that machine, so a stand with three logs opens one ssh connection, not three.

connections._comment: type local runs the reader on this machine. Use it for a backend you run yourself.
connections.name: local

connections._comment: type ssh runs it one hop away. The host key is NOT auto-accepted: ssh in by hand once first, or the reader fails with ssh's own message. identity is optional when your agent or ~/.ssh/config already answers; options are extra -o settings.
connections.name: staging

logs._comment: format names the SHAPE of a line, not an application. iso covers ISO-8601 and Python logging's default '2026-08-19 10:53:09,123' - so Django, Flask, FastAPI/uvicorn, Celery, Gunicorn, Odoo, Node/pino and Rails all read with this one. tz is the clock those timestamps were written by, and it is the setting worth checking first: plenty of backends (Odoo among them) log UTC, and on a machine that is not UTC every line then parses hours into the past and matches no window at all. envs must be spelled exactly as in users.json: that string is what ties a log to the windows opened against it. 'env' is accepted for a single one. default: true means a bare --server-log picks it.
logs.name: app

logs._comment: type docker follows a container instead of a file (docker logs -f), run through this log's connection. The application aliases - django, fastapi, node, odoo, rails, go... - each point at one of the shapes, and read better in a config file than the shape's own name.
logs.name: app

logs._comment: Several logs per environment is the point - this one is not a default, so ask for it: --server-log=app,nginx. A name has to be unique within an environment, which is why 'app' can repeat above. The slash shape is nginx's error log and Go's standard log package.
logs.name: nginx

logs._comment: type journal follows systemd. unit '*' (or no unit) means the whole journal. The syslog shape matches what journalctl prints.
logs.name: system

logs._comment: No preset fits? Give timestamp and level yourself and any backend works. 'regex' must capture the value in one group, 'format' is a strptime pattern or the literal "iso" / "clf", and 'tz' is local/utc/+HH:MM for lines carrying no offset. A line with no timestamp inherits the previous line's, which is what keeps a stack trace attached to its own message. format 'none' is for logs with no timestamps at all - every line is stamped as it arrives.
logs.name: worker

logs._comment: type http reads a line-oriented stream (plain text or server-sent events) and ignores 'connection'. headers is where a token goes - which is why this file is git-ignored.
logs.name: gateway
